title: Places little George played: cabarets, Franklin Street and Jackson Avenue
summary: Charlotte recalls where little George played in the 1920s, including a Jackson Avenue place with Steve Lewis where his gold watch was stolen.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: We have a couple more minutes to take on here.
What's some places you remember where Lil' George played at? Other than the music box when he was on that Jitney job. I know he stayed there a few years.
I know he stayed in the WPA band long.
I mean before that. He played all down in the... About the 20s. Before we left here in 1929.
He went on the road several times.
You ought to be telling somebody. Entertainment's cabaret.
They used to play on the roof guard. George used to play.

Not only that. He played at... This is where his gold watch was stolen. They're always stealing from him. Is it Tin Roof? Not Tin Roof. No, no. This place was right off of Jackson Avenue. On this fellow who died in the crazy house. He's a piano player. I know just where you're making. Steve... Steve Lewis. Steve Lewis was his piano player. Yes, Steve Lewis. Steve Lewis. And they played at this. This was some name. What can I think of this? This is a hot place. Southern... Yes. Mary Gordon. No. No. No. No. It's Jackson Avenue. Right off of Jackson Avenue. I know. But it's right on Jackson Avenue.
That's right. I'm afraid. No living there.

Around the corner. Right off Jackson. I think it was on Living Day or Saratoga. That's right. I know. I know. I know. I know what I'm showing you about the hall that.
